rv.q: If you allow the story and the characters who tell it to wash over you, you will find Clyde's to be as satisfying as one of Montrellous's memorable creations, say "curried quail egg salad with mint on oven-fresh cranberry pecan multigrain bread."
There’s a quirky edge to Oil Lamp’s production that gives audiences a few surprises while staying true to the heart of this enduring classic.
It is a wonderful story and this one is fun to see live and in Glenview.

I'm sure for many families out there, seeing this abridged radio-play adaptation of a landmark film has become an honored tradition over the years, and, if anything, I'm glad to have partaken in it this year just to see what keeps bringing people back, even if I don't think I'll be among them.

cn.t: Critics find this holiday radio play charming and atmospheric, with the intimate Oil Lamp setting a natural fit for Bedford Falls. Reception is mostly warm, though some feel the format overshadows the source material's magic.
